mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission matrix definition would allow roles to have arbitrary permissions, violating least-privilege and role-specific access controls. The constraint is foundational to all permission-based assertions.

Removing this constraint allows an application's assigned officer to be the same user as the applicant, violating the no-self-approval and conflict-of-interest prevention rules fundamental to the feature.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SelfAssignmentViolation { some app: LoanApplication | app.assigned_officer = app.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows applications to exist without an initial audit entry, violating the audit-completeness invariant that every application creation must be recorded in the audit log.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingInitialAudit { some app: LoanApplication | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.application = app and ae.previous_status = none }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows invalid state transitions (e.g., pending → approved, or transitions from terminal states), violating the state-machine invariant documented in FR-009.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InvalidTransition { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.previous_status = Pending and ae.new_status = Approved }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this constraint allows non-assigned officers or applicants to create audit entries for status transitions, or allows an officer to decide their own application, violating both assignment and self-approval rules.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthorizedDecision { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.previous_status != none and ae.actor != ae.application.assigned_officer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this constraint allows an applicant to submit multiple in-flight (pending/under_review) applications simultaneously, violating the one-in-flight rule that prevents concurrent application flooding.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MultipleInFlight { some user: User | some disj app1, app2: LoanApplication | app1.applicant = user and app2.applicant = user and (app1.status = Pending or app1.status = UnderReview) and (app2.status = Pending or app2.status = UnderReview) }
